accreditation.title: Researcher Accreditation
accreditation.description: Verify your identity as a researcher to publish papers and write peer reviews on PEvO.

about.title: About PEvO
about.whatIsDescription: PEvO (Publish and Evaluate Openly) is an open platform for scientific publication and interactive peer evaluation. Papers, reviews, and votes are recorded on a permanent public record that no single entity controls, making the entire scientific discourse transparent, permanent, and verifiable.
about.whyDescription: Traditional academic publishing suffers from opaque peer review processes, paywalled access, slow publication cycles, and concentrated gatekeeping power. PEvO addresses these issues by making publication instant, review transparent, and access unrestricted.
about.noPaywallsDesc: All research is freely accessible to everyone, permanently.
about.transparentReviewDesc: Reviews and ratings are publicly recorded and verifiable by anyone.
about.noGatekeepersDesc: Accredited researchers publish directly. No editor bottleneck.
about.immutableRecordDesc: Published work cannot be altered or censored after the fact.
about.howItWorksCaption: PEvO replaces the gatekept journal model with open, transparent publishing and evaluation.
about.step1Desc: Write your paper in Markdown or upload a PDF. Your name and timestamp are permanently recorded on the public record.
about.step2Desc: Accredited researchers write structured peer reviews with ratings on methodology, novelty, clarity, and significance. Anonymous reviewing is supported.
about.step3Desc: The community votes on papers and reviews. Reputation scores are computed transparently from your published activity: publications, reviews, votes, citations, and accreditation status.
about.architectureCaption: PEvO is built on the Hive network and IPFS for permanent, distributed storage that no single entity controls.
about.accreditationDesc: Anyone can read and vote on PEvO. To publish papers and write reviews, researchers verify their identity through an institutional email. This accreditation is recorded as a public attestation, building trust without centralized control.
about.openSourceDesc: PEvO is non-profit, AGPL-3.0-licensed, and fully forkable. The reputation algorithm is transparent and configurable. All data lives on a permanent public record that anyone can read. There are no tokens, no paywalls, no vendor lock-in.
about.comparisonSubtitle: PEvO combines the full open, transparent, decentralized stack. Other platforms cover parts well.
about.comparisonFooter: Based on publicly available information as of April 2026. Sci-Hub and Sci-Net are access platforms, not publishing platforms — features outside their scope are marked n/a. Hover over any cell for details.
about.tip_Publishing_pevo: Publish directly to the permanent record — no editorial gate, no waiting
about.tip_Publishing_arxiv: Moderated: submissions screened before posting, some rejections
about.tip_Publishing_scienceopen: Basic screening, some collections are editorially curated
about.tip_Publishing_octopus: Publish any research output instantly, no gatekeeping
about.tip_Ratings_pevo: 6 vote levels from Strong endorsement to Strong reject, weighted by reviewer reputation
about.tip_Ratings_f1000: Structured referee reports with recommendation levels
about.tip_Ratings_scienceopen: Star ratings available, but not mandatory on all content
about.tip_Ratings_octopus: Quality ratings on individual outputs, still evolving
about.tip_Ratings_traditional: Accept/revise/reject decisions — rarely quantitative or public
about.tip_OpenSource_pevo: AGPL-3.0-licensed, all code and algorithms are public and forkable
about.tip_Immutable_pevo: Every publication is a signed transaction on a public, append-only record (Hive)
about.tip_NonProfit_pevo: No fees to publish, read, or review — funded by community
about.tip_NonProfit_arxiv: Free to read and submit, funded by Cornell and grants
about.tip_NonProfit_f1000: Author-side publication fees (APCs) for some services
about.tip_NonProfit_octopus: Free to use, funded by UK Research and Innovation
about.tip_NonProfit_scihub: Free access — operates outside copyright law
about.tip_NonProfit_scinet: Free access with optional token incentives for uploaders
about.tip_NonProfit_traditional: Subscription paywalls or author-pays open access (APCs)
about.tip_Transparent_pevo: All reviews are public and signed (or pseudonymous by choice)
about.tip_Transparent_f1000: Published referee reports visible alongside papers
about.tip_Transparent_scienceopen: Open peer review with published reviewer identities
about.tip_Transparent_octopus: Reviews are published openly alongside research outputs
about.tip_Versioning_pevo: Continuation-chain versioning with linked corrections and diff tracking
about.tip_Versioning_arxiv: Version history (v1, v2, …) with all versions accessible
about.tip_Versioning_f1000: Revised versions after review, but limited linking
about.tip_Versioning_scienceopen: Some version tracking, not systematic across all content
about.tip_Versioning_octopus: Outputs can be revised but linking is limited
about.tip_Versioning_traditional: Errata and corrigenda exist but are poorly linked to original
about.tip_Orcid_pevo: ORCID linking supported, not yet mandatory
about.tip_Orcid_arxiv: ORCID can be linked to author profiles
about.tip_Orcid_f1000: ORCID integration for authors and reviewers
about.tip_Accreditation_pevo: Verified researcher identity via institutional email or ORCID
about.tip_Accreditation_f1000: Invited reviewers, but no systematic public accreditation
about.tip_Accreditation_scienceopen: Some reviewer verification, varies by collection
about.tip_Accreditation_traditional: Editors select reviewers, credentials not publicly verified
about.tip_Anonymous_pevo: Built-in anonymous review via encrypted proxy — reviewer identity protected with time-limited mapping
about.tip_Anonymous_f1000: Named reviews by default, some journals allow anonymity
about.tip_Anonymous_scienceopen: Open review default, anonymity available in some cases
about.tip_Anonymous_pubpeer: Anonymous commenting is the default mode
about.tip_Anonymous_octopus: Named reviews default, anonymity being considered
about.tip_Anonymous_scinet: Anonymous uploading with watermark removal — no identity required
about.tip_Anonymous_traditional: Single- or double-blind review is standard

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with PEvO
gettingStarted.description: A step-by-step guide for scientists new to open publishing on PEvO.
gettingStarted.step1Description: Hive Keychain is a browser extension that securely manages your account keys. It is required to sign publications and reviews on PEvO.
gettingStarted.step2Description: You need a free Hive account to interact with PEvO. If you do not have one, you can create one through several services, or join our Discord and we will walk you through it.
gettingStarted.step3Description: Click the "Sign In" button in the header. Enter your Hive username and sign a challenge to prove account ownership.
gettingStarted.step4Description: To publish papers and write reviews, you need to verify your researcher identity. You can do this through institutional email verification or by receiving vouches from accredited colleagues.
gettingStarted.step5Description: Write your paper in Markdown or upload a PDF. Add metadata (title, keywords, co-authors) and publish to the permanent record.
gettingStarted.step6Description: Read papers by other researchers and write structured peer reviews. Rate papers on methodology, novelty, clarity, and significance.
gettingStarted.step7Description: Your reputation score is computed from your published activity. Publish quality research, write thoughtful reviews, and earn citations to grow your score.
gettingStarted.tip1: Your Hive account keys are important - never share your active or owner keys.
gettingStarted.tip2: Published papers are stored permanently on Hive and cannot be deleted. You can publish revised versions that link back to the original.
gettingStarted.tip3: Anonymous reviewing is available for accredited researchers who want to protect their identity.
gettingStarted.tip4: You can use LaTeX math notation in your papers using standard $ and $$ delimiters.
gettingStarted.tip5: Large papers (over 64KB) should be uploaded as PDFs, which are stored on IPFS.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about PEvO and open science.
faq.a1: PEvO (Publish and Evaluate Openly) is an open platform for scientific publication and interactive peer evaluation. Papers, reviews, and votes are recorded on a permanent public record that no single entity controls, making the entire scientific discourse transparent, permanent, and verifiable.
faq.a2: Yes. PEvO is completely free. There are no transaction fees, so publishing, reviewing, and voting cost nothing. PEvO is non-profit and open source.
faq.a3: PEvO is built on Hive, an open network designed for content and social applications. It processes updates in 3 seconds, has no transaction fees, and stores data across thousands of independent nodes worldwide. If PEvO the website disappeared tomorrow, every paper and review would still exist on every Hive node.
faq.a4: No. PEvO is completely free to use. There are no fees for publishing, reviewing, or voting. You just need a free Hive account and the Hive Keychain browser extension.
faq.a5: Hive Keychain is a browser extension that securely stores your Hive account keys and signs your publications and reviews. You never have to share your private keys with PEvO.
faq.q6: What is accreditation and why do I need it?
faq.a6: Accreditation verifies that you are an active researcher. It is required to publish papers and write reviews. You can get accredited by verifying your institutional email or by receiving vouches from accredited colleagues (Web of Trust).
faq.a7: Papers are always attributed to the publishing account. However, peer reviews can be submitted anonymously through a platform proxy account. The reviewer's identity is stored encrypted and can only be revealed through a governance process.
faq.a8: Papers are stored permanently on Hive and cannot be deleted. This is by design - it ensures the integrity of the scientific record. If you need to revise a paper, you can publish an updated version that links to the original. All previous versions remain accessible, and reviews stay attached to the version they were written for.
faq.a9: Papers can be written directly in Markdown (with LaTeX math support) or uploaded as PDFs. PDFs are stored on IPFS for permanent, distributed access. Short papers can live entirely as Markdown posts.
faq.q10: How does the reputation system work?
faq.a10: Reputation scores are computed from your published activity: the number and quality of publications, peer reviews written, citations received, community votes, and accreditation status. The algorithm is transparent and configurable.
faq.a11: Yes. PEvO is AGPL-3.0-licensed and fully forkable. The source code, reputation algorithm, and all data are public. There are no tokens, no paywalls, and no vendor lock-in.
faq.q12: How do I cite a PEvO paper?
faq.a12: Each paper has a unique identifier (author/permlink) and a permanent URL. You can cite PEvO papers like any other online publication, using the author names, title, date, and PEvO URL.
faq.ctaDescription: We are here to help. Reach out to us directly.
